#### BLOCKER — F1

> (6) apply to screens in attention order — gate, running, session, ack
- **Question**: The design applies the presentation layer (footer + `?` help overlay per D7) to the ack screen, and the spec requires "Every interactive screen SHALL offer a help overlay, toggled by `?`" while also requiring "The presentation layer SHALL NOT alter decision semantics, key semantics". On the any-key ack screen every key — including `?` — currently acks and exits, so composing reduceHelpOverlay above it (D7's routing has no ack carve-out: no text-entry context exists there, so `?` falls through to "otherwise `?` opens") either changes that screen's any-key contract or leaves the spec unsatisfied. Is the ack shell in the overlay/footer contract at all, and if so what does `?` do against the any-key ack? This is a product decision the artifacts must make, not something the repo can answer.
- **Code evidence**: tui-ack-screen.ts:15-16 documents "Any key returns; an exhausted script also resolves"; its useInput handler (lines 47-54) acks on every key with no key discrimination, so there is no unbound key for `?` to take. design.md's own Context lists "the any-key ack shell (`tui-ack-screen.ts`)" among "The interactive surfaces", so the spec's "every interactive screen" clause reaches it by the design's own framing, yet the spec's parenthetical enumeration "(running, gate, and session screens alike)" omits it — the artifacts disagree on whether ack is in scope, and no repo fact resolves it.
- **Resolution**: edited — Verified real: tui-ack-screen.ts:47-50 acks on every key with no discrimination, so the spec's 'Every interactive screen SHALL offer a help overlay, toggled by ?' is unsatisfiable on ack without breaking its own presentation-invariants requirement. Resolved by the least-surprise default — the any-key contract wins: spec.md help-overlay requirement now scopes to 'every interactive screen with its own key bindings' and explicitly exempts the any-key ack shell ('? acks like any other key'); design.md D7 adds the routing carve-out ('the any-key ack shell is not composed with the overlay') and migration step 6 marks ack as framing-only. The footer requirement needs no exemption — ack's one affordance ('any key — back') is exactly what its footer lists.

#### MATERIAL — F2

> Each interactive screen SHALL split its content into an append-only history region and a live region.
- **Question**: The spec scopes the Static/live split to every interactive screen, but the design delivers it only on the running screen (D6 derives history rows from the run folds; migration step 7: "`tui-history` Static split on the running screen"). Gate rows mutate in place (checkbox toggles, redirects, blocker answers) and session rows are re-read each loop, so an append-only region there is either vacuous or harmful (a gate item emitted to Static would freeze its `[ ]`/`[x]` mark). Should the requirement be scoped to screens with finalized rows (the running screen) instead of "each interactive screen"?
- **Code evidence**: tui-gate.ts:83-98 renders toggleable `[x]`/`[ ]` item rows that change on later keys (gate-session-state.ts lines 103-110 toggle/redirect), so gate rows are live-mutating, not finalized; tui-session-picker.ts's loop re-reads rows from storage every iteration; run-view.ts:82-108 is the only screen with append-only content (burndown rows, filed findings, done slots) and it is what D6/migration step 7 target. The spec's example rows ("per-round burndown rows, filed finding rows, completed agent rows") are all running-screen rows, confirming the over-broad scoping is textual, not intentional coverage.
- **Resolution**: edited — Verified: tui-gate.ts:83-98 renders live-mutating toggle rows ([x]/[ ] marks, redirects, answers) and the session screen re-reads rows each loop iteration, so an append-only region there would freeze stale state. Spec requirement rescoped to 'Each interactive screen that renders finalized history entries SHALL split…; screens whose content is entirely live (the gate's decision surfaces, the session list) render wholly in the live region' — matching what D6/migration step 7 actually deliver (running screen only). Scenarios were already running-screen rows; no design edit needed.

#### MATERIAL — F1

> The existing stack cannot compute East Asian/emoji display width — `padEnd` pads by UTF-16 code units (today's `finding.class.padEnd(8)`).
- **Question**: D3 justifies two new direct deps with a categorical 'cannot' that the repo contradicts: renderer.ts exports a wide-char-aware truncateVisible (WIDE_RANGES covering CJK/Hangul/emoji + Intl.Segmenter graphemes, 'no dependency'). The pad gap is real, and string-width may still win on ZWJ/combining marks (the design's own risk bullet names those as beyond the local table) — but should D3 be corrected to state the true decision space (reuse the exported truncateVisible vs add deps), per the repo's 'is it already in this codebase' minimality gate, before apply?
- **Code evidence**: Read sdd-runner/src/renderer.ts:180-228: WIDE_RANGES spans 0x2e80–0xa4cf (CJK), 0xac00–0xd7a3 (Hangul), 0x1f300–0x1f64f and 0x1f900–0x1f9ff (emoji); isWideCode(); graphemesOf() using Intl.Segmenter; exported truncateVisible(line, maxWidth, segmenter) whose doc comment reads 'Wide-char-aware truncation (D10): truncate by visible display width so wide characters and emoji never break alignment — local `Intl.Segmenter` + a range table, no dependency.' So the existing stack DOES compute East Asian/emoji display width for truncation; only width-aware padding is missing (finding.class.padEnd(8) at run-view.ts:88 and watch-view.ts:58 pads by code units). The Non-Goal 'no edits to renderer.ts' does not bar importing the exported helper. No prior finding (F1–F11) covers this; F3 was only about lockfile-vs-manifest growth.
- **Resolution**: edited — design.md D3 rewritten to state the true decision space: renderer.ts already exports truncateVisible (wide-char-aware truncation via local range table + Intl.Segmenter, renderer.ts:212), but computes no display-width padding, exports no width function, and the Non-Goal bars editing frozen renderer.ts to add one — reuse would mean duplicating its range table, and one aligned row padded by one width authority and truncated by another would drift. D3 now makes tui-panels the single width authority (string-width measures — covering the combining marks/ZWJ the local table misses — cli-truncate truncates by the same measure), keeps the two direct deps on those accurate grounds, and notes renderer.ts keeps its local helper untouched for the frozen non-TTY path. Verified: isWideCode/graphemesOf are module-private; only truncateVisible is exported.

#### MATERIAL — F1

> D1: "`tui-width.ts` — `useTerminalWidth()` hook + `WidthFeed` scripted seam. No module tracks width changes." D5: "`useTerminalWidth()` reads `useStdout()` and subscribes to `resize`, replacing the mount-time capture and the gate's hardcoded 100."
- **Question**: Ink 7.1.1 — the exact version locked and installed — already exports `useWindowSize`, a hook that does precisely what D5 describes building (reads `useStdout()`, subscribes to `resize`, re-renders on change). Should `tui-width.ts` build on the stock hook (reducing the module to the `WidthFeed` seam / width-prop injection), or is a hand-rolled duplicate justified — and if justified, why does D1 justify the module with "No module tracks width changes" when an installed dependency ships exactly that?
- **Code evidence**: Repo-answered; consistency gap, not product judgment. node_modules/ink/build/index.d.ts:35 exports `useWindowSize` (ink@7.1.1 per bun.lock:1058); node_modules/ink/build/hooks/use-window-size.js:7-20 implements exactly "const { stdout } = useStdout(); … stdout.on('resize', onResize)" returning {columns, rows}; ink itself already re-renders on resize (node_modules/ink/build/ink.js:265 `options.stdout.on('resize', this.resized)`), confirming D5's own framing that only the outside-the-tree width capture is broken — which the stock hook fixes by construction. Grepped sdd-runner/src for `useWindowSize|useTerminalWidth`: no matches, so nothing conflicts with adopting it. D5's scripted-resize concern is independently solvable: ink-testing-library's fake stdout has a getter-only `columns` fixed at 100 (node_modules/ink-testing-library/build/index.js:3-6, verifying D5's claim), but live `render` accepts an injectable stdout (the AckMount seam pattern, tui-ack-screen.ts:26) whose columns can change and emit 'resize', so the WidthFeed seam does not require reimplementing the hook. AGENTS.md Key Conventions ("does the stdlib or an installed dependency already do it … Only then write something new") make the unacknowledged duplicate a MATERIAL design-grounding gap; it is not a BLOCKER because the design is implementable as written and no invariant breaks.
- **Resolution**: edited — design.md now bases `tui-width.ts` on ink's stock `useWindowSize` (verified: ink@7.1.1 locked at bun.lock:1058 exports it at node_modules/ink/build/index.d.ts:35; use-window-size.js:7-20 implements useStdout + resize subscription + rerender, with non-TTY size fallback in utils.js getWindowSize). D1's bullet drops the false 'No module tracks width changes' justification — the module is now scoped to width-prop plumbing + the WidthFeed scripted seam over the stock hook, no hand-rolled subscription. #### MATERIAL — F1

> Every interactive screen with its own key bindings SHALL offer a help overlay, toggled by `?`, listing that screen's keys with their meanings. [...] In text-entry contexts (veto redirect, blocker answer, creation-form fields) `?` SHALL be inserted as literal input text and SHALL NOT open the overlay.
- **Question**: Is the help-overlay requirement satisfiable on the creation-form sub-screen, which has its own key bindings (Tab/Enter/Esc) but is permanently in a text-entry context, so `?` can never open the overlay there?
- **Code evidence**: Answered from the repo — it is not satisfiable there, by construction. session-create-form.ts:65-80: reduceCreateForm always routes printable input into the active field's buffer (line 79 `if (input.length > 0) return { kind: 'state', state: editBuffer(state, buffer + normalizeInput(input)) }`), and CreateFormState.field (lines 14-15) is `'title' | 'description'` with no non-field state, so `?` is always literal input — exactly what the requirement's own text-entry clause mandates, and what design D7 relies on ('creation-form fields ... all already reducer-owned'). tui-session-screen.ts:23 makes `create` a distinct screen state rendering its own key surface (hint line '(Tab) switch field · (Enter) start · (Esc) back' at line 197). The requirement's own structure shows sub-screens are in scope — the delete-confirmation sub-screen needed an explicit exemption ('The session screen's delete-confirmation sub-screen carries the same exemption') — yet the creation form is unexempted while its `?`-toggle is unreachable, leaving the SHALL silently undeliverable on that one surface. No contract breaks (unlike round-1's ack shell, where following the overlay rule would have broken the any-key contract), and design D7 already prescribes the right behavior, so this is a spec-wording fix, not a product-judgment gap: extend the exemption sentence to name the creation form (its `?` stays literal; its bindings ride the footer), mirroring the ack carve-out. No design edit needed — D7 already routes creation-form `?` to text.
- **Resolution**: edited — Extended the help-overlay requirement's exemption sentence in specs/sdd-runner-tui-presentation/spec.md to name the session screen's creation-form sub-screen: it is permanently a text-entry context, so `?` is always inserted as literal input text and never opens the overlay there, while its bindings remain listed in the footer — mirroring the existing ack-shell and delete-confirmation carve-outs. Verified before editing: session-create-form.ts:14-15 (`field` is always 'title' | 'description', no non-field state) and session-create-form.ts:79 (every printable char, `?` included, routes into the active buffer); tui-session-screen.ts:23 makes 'create' a distinct screen state. Design D7 already routes creation-form `?` to literal text, so no design edit was needed.

#### NITPICK — F3

> When color is disabled (`NO_COLOR` set, or the terminal cannot render color), interactive screens SHALL remain structurally identical to the colored rendering
- **Question**: Can 'the terminal cannot render color' ever fire, given mode selection never mounts the interactive screens on a dumb terminal in the first place?
- **Code evidence**: Answered from the repo — effectively unreachable for the dumb case, harmless but slightly misleading as written. The binding (unarchived) tui-wiring requirement 'Interactive terminals get the TUI' mounts the TUI only 'whenever stdout and stdin are TTYs, no CI environment variable is set, and the terminal type is not `dumb`' (openspec/changes/sdd-runner-tui-wiring/specs/sdd-runner-tui/spec.md:7), and design Context confirms '`renderModeFor` never gives a non-TTY sink the TUI'. So a color-incapable dumb terminal never displays an interactive screen; the clause's only reachable reading is a TTY that mounts the screens but cannot render color, and the scenarios already scope the requirement to 'while a screen is displayed'. The parallel proposal wording '`NO_COLOR` / `TERM=dumb` degrade to today's monochrome' is accurate only in the sense that TERM=dumb gets today's line renderer (byte stream untouched) — no monochrome screen is ever rendered there. Cosmetic: scoping the parenthetical to displayed screens, or naming `NO_COLOR` only, removes the invitation to implement a dumb-terminal color check that can never fire inside `colorModeFor(env)`.
- **Resolution**: evidence-answered — Yes, the clause can fire — but not on a dumb terminal, on a colorless non-dumb one. The wiring delta mounts the interactive screens whenever stdout and stdin are TTYs, no CI variable is set, and the terminal type is not `dumb` (openspec/changes/sdd-runner-tui-wiring/specs/sdd-runner-tui/spec.md:7) — it excludes only `dumb`, not color-incapable terminals. A non-dumb colorless TTY (e.g. TERM=vt100) therefore displays the interactive screens with color unavailable, which is exactly the reachable reading the parenthetical covers; the reviewer's unreachability analysis holds only for the TERM=dumb case, which the clause never names. The requirement is satisfiable as written and invites no dead dumb-terminal check inside colorModeFor(env), so no artifact change is needed.

#### NITPICK — F1

> THEN a footer listing that screen's keys is visible at all times
- **Question**: While the help overlay is open, must the footer remain visible beneath it, or may the overlay occupy the live region (key discoverability then being served by the overlay's own key list)? Neither artifact pins the footer/overlay stacking during overlay-open.
- **Code evidence**: Attempted to answer from the repository before asking: today's footers are static lines inside each screen's rendered body (tui-session-screen.ts:177 list footer, :197 create-form footer, :187 confirmDelete affordance line; tui-ack-screen.ts:71 '(any key) back to sessions'; run-view.ts:67 'q to stop' rides the status line), so a footer survives re-presentation only if the composing layer keeps rendering it. design.md D6 places 'footer' in the live region and D7 places the overlay in the live region too ('The overlay renders in the live region; dismissal restores the frame exactly') — both claim the same region and neither states which wins while the overlay is open; docs/architecture/sdd-pipeline.md has no overlay content to consult (verified headings ## Commands / ## Live rendering / ## Gate decisions). The repo cannot answer this; it is a one-clause product choice, cosmetic in impact either way.
- **Resolution**: assumed — Footer stays visible during overlay-open: the overlay renders as an inset panel within the live region's content area, above the footer, rather than replacing the full frame. This is the only reading consistent with the spec's own wording — 'SHALL display a persistent footer' plus the scenario's 'visible at all times' carry no overlay-open exception, and the help-overlay requirement explicitly enumerates its exemptions (ack shell, delete-confirmation sub-screen) without excusing footer visibility. Key discoverability while the overlay is open is served by both the overlay's own key list and the footer. The stacking mechanics remain an implementation detail of tui-chrome; D6 (footer in live region) and D7 (overlay in live region, 'dismissal restores the frame exactly') stay coherent under this default.
